1 The petitioner is a minor child who had suffered injuries in an accident when he was knocked down by a two wheeler bearing Regn.No.TN 20 P 6336.
Seeking compensation, he moved the Tribunal.
The disability of the minor child was assessed at 6%.
The Tribunal had reckoned the compensation payable under the head permanent disability at Rs.4,000/- for every percentage of disability and has awarded Rs.24,000/-.
In all, it had awarded Rs.82,000/-.
2.Challenging the award of compensation payable under the head 'permanent disability' alone, the claimant has come before this Court.
3.The first respondent, the owner of the offending vehicle remained ex- parte before the Tribunal.

Hence, notice to the first respondent is dispensed with.
4.Mr.J.Chandran, learned counsel is already on record for the second respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

5.The only contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that as per the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mallikarjun Vs.Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another [(2014) 14 SCC 396 = 2013 (2) TANMAC 338] for permanent disability up to 10%,
Rs.1,00,000/- need to be paid, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs.Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another [(2014) 14 SCC 396 = 2013 (2) TANMAC 338]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel submitted that that the second respondent has not demonstrated any particular circumstance to reduce the compensation payable to any sum below Rs.1,00,000/-.
6.This Court concurs with the statement of the learned counsel for the appellant.
7.Accordingly, the compensation payable under the head permanent disability is modified and enhanced from Rs.24,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads are just and reasonable and hence, the same are confirmed.
Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.82,400/- to Rs.1,58,400/-, break-up as follows - https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  Sl.

8.With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.82,400/- is hereby enhanced to Rs.1,58,400/- together with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

This Court is informed that the second respondent /Insurance Company had already deposited the sum originally awarded by the Tribunal and it is now https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis required to deposit the differential sum with interest, less interest payable for 80 days, within six (6) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the award amount, now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.
The appellant is directed to pay the necessary Court Fee, if any, on the enhanced award amount.
No costs.
